newsitem.title: USA: GM names new small car operations head.
newsitem.headline: GM names new small car operations head.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday it named Mark T. Hogan as general manager of operations for its North American Operations Small Car Group.

The 45-year-old Hogan was previously president and managing director of GM do Brasil, the unit in charge of GM's operations in Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. He succeeds James R. Wiemels, who was appointed chairman and managing director of GM's Australian subsidiary, Holden's Automotive.

Hogan, whose appointment is effective May 1, will report to Donald Hackworth, the group executive who oversees GM's Midsize and Luxury Car Group, as well as the Small Car Group. Although Hogan is with GM's north american operations unit, his new role will also involve coordinating GM's increasingly global vehicle platforms.

After several financial assignments, Hogan served as general manager of New United Motor Manufacturing, Inc., GM's joint venture with Toyota Motor Corp in Fremont, Calif. He had been in Brazil since 1992.
To replace Hogan, GM named Frederick A. Henderson to head up GM do Brasil. Henderson, 38, had been general manager of Delphi Saginaw Steering Systems. He will join GM's International Strategy Board.

Paul J. Tosch, 56, was named general manager of Delphi Saginaw Steering Systems, succeeding Henderson. Tosch had been general manager of Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems. He will continue to serve on the Delphi Strategy Board.

Rodney O'Neal was named a GM vice president and general manager of Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems, succeeding Tosch. O'Neal, 43, has been general director of Warehousing and Distribution for GM's Service Parts Operations. He will join the Delphi Strategy Board.
Including O'Neal, GM now has four African-Americans among its more than 40 vice presidents.
